thesis: A lamp is a slow heat engine you can watch: wax warms, loses density, rises as a blob, cools, sinks, and the glow of the bulb makes the whole thing a light source, not just a picture.
job: arrive and see a lamp already running (no empty start)
watch blobs rise, stretch, pinch off, merge, sink
switch the lamp on/off (bulb heats or cools; wax slows, settles, gathers at base when cold)
turn heat up or down and see speed and blob size change
poke or tap a blob / drag to stir
room ambience reacts (lamp glow lights the surroundings)
works on phone and desktop, keyboard reachable, reduced motion respected

principles: metaballs: sum of radial fields, threshold gives merging surface
buoyancy depends on temperature; heat from bottom, cooling at top
steps: render on low-res offscreen canvas, upscale with blur+contrast
update temperature, velocity, position each frame with dt
tricks: blur then contrast filter on canvas gives gooey merge cheaply
render field at 1/3 resolution and scale up for smoothness and speed
a pool blob at base that bleeds upward gives pinch-off look
tests: do two blobs bridge before they merge
does a blob slow near top
does cold lamp settle to a puddle

principles: glow comes from the bulb below, light falls off upward
translucency: wax brighter at edges (rim light), darker core
steps: base and cap in metal with highlights
tricks: radial glow behind lamp tinted by liquid colour
vertical gradient in liquid, hot at bottom
thin white vertical highlight on glass left
slight noise/grain avoided; use soft shadows
tests: can a stranger name it at a glance
does the lamp light the room

principles: controls are physical: switch, dial, swatches
state visible in the object itself
tricks: poke adds an impulse and heat to nearby blobs
tests: does every control change something visible

expectations: slow, hypnotic, 1 to 3 minutes to a full cycle on real lamps

kinds.name: classic rocket lamp
kinds.what: tapered glass, red wax in yellow liquid or orange in purple, metal base and cap

kinds.name: globe lamp
kinds.what: round glass globe on a short base

kinds.name: full-screen ambient lava
kinds.what: wax fills whole page as wallpaper

kinds.name: lava lamp with night room
kinds.what: lamp on a shelf and the wall lit by it

descriptions: glass narrows from base to top (about 1.9:1 bottom to top width)
lamp 40 to 55 percent of viewport height ratio ~ 1:2.6 width to height
behaviors: wax melts at bottom into a pool, rises as blob
tail stretches behind a rising blob then snaps
at the top blobs flatten, cool, sink

tokens.rise_speed: 10 to 40 px per second at medium heat

descriptions: wax is brighter than liquid, liquid is dim version of a hue
behaviors: bulb off dims glow and room

descriptions: temperature lags the bulb: warm up 6 to 12 s, cool down 10 to 20 s
horizontal drift is small noise, vertical dominates
behaviors: heat slider scales buoyancy and speed
off: temperature decays, blobs stop, sink, spread as puddle

anti_keywords.not: flat circles bouncing like a screensaver
anti_keywords.instead: metaball fields that bridge and pinch, with stretching tails
dark room lit by the lamp itself, colour from the liquid

anti_keywords.not: a control panel next to a canvas
anti_keywords.instead: switch, dial and swatches built into the lamp base and shelf
hot-to-cool gradient inside wax, rim light
glass highlight and lamp glow that follow bulb state

checks: do two blobs bridge before they merge
does a blob slow near the top and sink
does turning it off settle wax to a puddle and dim the room
does every control visibly change state
does it read as a lava lamp at a glance on desktop and at 375 px
no console errors, no external requests
